findings.body: A trailing YAML comment defeats named-job detection. In the new migration test's remaining workflow, changing `name: frontend-lint` to `name: frontend-lint # client check` makes this regex reject the name and record `lint` instead. Consequently, the deleted workflow's required `lint` check survives even though no remaining workflow produces it, blocking subsequent merges. GitHub uses the [job name](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#jobsjob_idname), not the comment or overridden job ID. Handle commented names correctly and extend the command-level regression test with this case.

findings.body: An absolute local origin bypasses refusal and restores `{owner}/{repo}` in both protection requests. These [gh API placeholders](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_api) resolve through repository selection or `GH_REPO`, so an unrelated GitHub remote can receive the protection update. The production exception exists solely for tests. Remove it and give command fixtures an explicit GitHub fetch URL with a local push URL, as the new origin-targeting test already does at tests/test_fix_forge_s_branch_protection_keeps_required.py:65–66.
findings.title: Simpler: test-only repository fallback → refuse unresolved origins

why: Forge's branch protection keeps required checks whose workflows a migration deletes, which blocks every later pull request once admins are enforced, and with two remotes and no gh default it can protect the wrong repo
